summary: Skamania County tower site: a 1924 camp, an L-4 tower dated 1930 or 1934 depending on source, staffed in 1955, removed in the 1960s; no source describes it today.

facts.design: L-4 cabin on a 15-foot wood tower with a 10-by-10-foot storage building below (Willhite); the Register says a 15-foot pole L-4 tower
facts.status_note: Removed in the early 1960s; a 1964 USGS party reported it destroyed

access.note: Road to the trailhead repaired at the end of 2019 after years of closure; route described on Willhite

visit.trail_note: Route from Randle along FR 23 (Cispus Road), then a signed road 5 miles up to the trailhead; hike 1.7 miles with 1,400 feet of gain, per Willhite

events.note: Lookout camp with a tent and probably a telephone
Newspapers reported plans for towers on Sunrise butte and two other buttes, each with a fire finder
Willhite dates the L-4 house on a 15-foot wood tower to 1930; a 1930 newspaper says a man had gone up to build a station
Frank Slagle stationed there for the summer and using a tent, per a July 25, 1930 Chehalis item
Register and firelookout.com date a 15-foot pole L-4 tower replacing the camp to 1934; conflicts with Willhite's 1930
A forest fire burned the telephone line to the lookout; the lookout was isolated but not in danger
Forest Service activated Sunrise as a ground observer post; Duane A. Priebe stationed there
Removed in the early 1960s per Willhite; the Register says removed in the 1960s, exact year not given
A USGS party in 1964 reported the lookout destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and firelookout.com date the L-4 tower replacing the 1924 camp to 1934. Willhite dates the L-4 house to 1930 from a 1930 newspaper item about building a station. The sources conflict and this record does not settle the date.

notes_for_editor: Thin on dates. The Register says the L-4 tower replaced the camp in 1934; Willhite says the house was built in 1930 and cites a 1930 newspaper that describes a station being built. Both are reported in the story and neither is resolved here. Staffing after 1955 is not documented, so the staffing as-of is the 1960s removal. The 'Hand railing is still there' caption is undated and does not name a structure, so no remains claim is made. Access 'public' is inferred from the described road and trail; the brief's 'unknown' is replaced. Willhite's undated claim that a young observer named William Boyer was the youngest lookout in the country is left out as unverified. A WebSearch for a Forest Service history found nothing usable.
